# Shareable Allure Report

Contract for the repository-owned report section every framework built by this skill gets (Mobile, Web, and each framework of Mobile + Web). Bootstrap builds the tooling, its labels and its fixture tests; real reports are generated later from saved results with `npm run report:share`. Nothing here reruns a test.

## 1. Output

`<framework root>/report/` (`<AutomationDir>/` for Mobile, `<AutomationDir>/Web/` for Web only, `<AutomationDir>/Mobile/` and `<AutomationDir>/Web/` for Mobile + Web, one report section each):

`report/` is shared by two producers: `npm run smoke` / `npm run regression` write one folder per run under `report/runs/` (`workbook-commands.md`, section 6), and `npm run report:share` writes cross-run snapshots under `report/snapshots/`. Both use the same builder (`scripts/report/`) and refresh the one dashboard `report/index.html`, which lists runs newest first, then snapshots.

```text
report/
  index.html                                  dashboard of runs and snapshots (regenerated by both commands)
  runs/<RUN_ID>/...                           per-run reports (workbook-commands.md)
  <RUN_ID>.zip
  snapshots/
    <SnapshotId>/                             snapshot-<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>
      index.html                              snapshot dashboard
      README.md                               how to open and share, limitations
      report-scope.json                       what is in the reports and why
      smoke/
        index.html                            Allure report of smoke results only
      regression/
        index.html                            epic index: every epic (workbook) with its stories (generated, not Allure)
        <WorkbookFolder>/
          index.html                          ONE Allure report with all of that epic's user stories
  <Application>-Allure-Reports-<YYYY-MM-DD>.zip   the snapshot's ZIP
```

- In the steps below, "`report/`" means the snapshot folder `report/snapshots/<SnapshotId>/`, and "`index.html`" the snapshot dashboard; step 9 also refreshes `report/index.html`.
- `report/` is generated output and Git-ignored. Each snapshot is written into a fresh temporary folder and moved into place only when every step passed, so a failed build never leaves a half-written report. Earlier runs and snapshots are never deleted or changed; only the dashboard is regenerated.
- It refuses to write when the target resolves outside `report/`, or when `report/` holds a file neither producer created (every produced folder has a `report-scope.json` with `"generator": "report:share"` or `"generator": "run-commands"`). It never touches `allure-results/`, `allure-report/`, `test-results/` or `reports/smoke/`.
- Use the word **Regression**, never "Normal", for the category everywhere.
- **Regression is reported per epic.** An epic is one approved workbook; its key is `<WorkbookFolder>` (the workbook file name without `.xlsx`, the same name as `src/tests/regression/<WorkbookFolder>/`). `regression/index.html` lists every epic; `regression/<WorkbookFolder>/index.html` is **one** Allure report holding all of that epic's executed user stories, grouped in Allure's Behaviors view by the `epic` → `feature` (story) labels. A run of only some stories (`npm run regression -- "<file>" US002 US003`) still goes into its epic's folder and is labelled "Partial epic: <n> of <m> stories". There are no per-story report folders.

## 2. Run metadata (written at bootstrap, used by every run)

Execution type is never inferred from a testcase ID or from a file name pattern alone. Every result carries explicit labels, added once in the shared hooks:

| Label | Value | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `executionType` | `smoke` or `regression` | `EXECUTION_TYPE` env var: `smoke:run` sets `smoke`; `scripts/run.ps1` and the Jenkins regression path set `regression`; unset → the label is `unknown` |
| `runId` | unique per run | `RUN_ID` env var (`regression-<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>`, or the smoke build ID); unset → generated in the hook from the worker start time |
| `specFile` | spec path relative to the framework root (`src/tests/regression/<WorkbookFolder>/US-002. <Story title>.test.ts`) | the test's file (Mocha `test.file`, Playwright `testInfo.file`) |
| `storyId` / `storyName` | `US002` / the top-level `describe` title after the ID | the spec's `describe('<StoryId> <story name>')` |
| `testCaseId` | `TC_...` | `testCaseIdOf(title)` (already used for `tms`) |
| `platform`, `environment` | `android` / `ios` / `chromium`..., `qa` / `uat`... | config (`PLATFORM`, Playwright project name, `TEST_ENV`) |
| `workbook` | approved workbook file name | `WORKBOOK` env var set by the run scripts; else `<WorkbookFolder>.xlsx` from the spec's folder `src/tests/regression/<WorkbookFolder>/`; else absent |
| `epic` | `<WorkbookFolder>` (workbook file name without `.xlsx`) | the `workbook` label without `.xlsx`; absent when `workbook` is absent |
| `feature` | `<StoryId> <story name>` | the spec's top-level `describe` title, so Allure's Behaviors view shows epic → story → testcase |

Mobile: `allureReporter.addLabel(name, value)` in `beforeTest` of `wdio.shared.conf.ts`. Web: `allure.label(name, value)` (allure-playwright) in the base fixture. Both follow "Method rules".

Raw results are kept per run:

- regression: `scripts/run.ps1` copies `allure-results/` and a `run.json` (runId, executionType, runType, stories, workbook, platform, environment, startedAt, finishedAt, timeZone, exitCode) to `test-results/allure-archive/<RunId>/` after every real run;
- runs that do not go through `run.ps1` (Web, iOS, any direct run): `npm run test:regression -- <runner args>` (`scripts/report/run-regression.mjs`) sets `EXECUTION_TYPE=regression` and `RUN_ID`, runs the framework's own runner (`wdio run config/wdio.<platform>.conf.ts` or `npx playwright test`) with the given arguments, then archives the results and `run.json` the same way. A plain `npx playwright test` / `npm run test:<platform>` still works, but its results are labelled `unknown` and `report:share` refuses them until the user names their type;
- smoke: `smoke:run` already keeps `reports/smoke/<WorkbookName>/<BuildId>/allure-results/`, and writes the same `run.json` there with `executionType: smoke` and the build's decision.

## 3. Command

`npm run report:share -- [--source latest|archive] [--runs <RunId,...>] [--since <date>] [--application "<name>"] [--date <YYYY-MM-DD>] [--include-screenshots] [--allow-mixed-platforms]`

Code in `scripts/report/build-share-report.mjs` (plain Node, no new dependency; uses the project's own Allure CLI through `npx allure`) with device- and browser-free fixture tests in `scripts/report/__tests__/`. Every function logs (automation-setup "Method rules").

| Source mode | Includes | Labelled as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `latest` (default) | the most recent run of each execution type: the newest archive run of each type (or `allure-results/` when it has no archive yet) | "Single run <RunId>, <date>" per section |
| `archive` | every archived run (filtered by `--runs` / `--since`), combined into a latest-outcome snapshot | "Snapshot of N runs, <first> to <last>" on every page |

## 4. Steps the command performs

1. **Inspect reporting.** Read the Allure CLI version (`npx allure --version`) and whether `allure generate --help` lists `--single-file`. Read `package.json` scripts and the source folders. Print what it found.
2. **Collect results** from the chosen sources: `*-result.json` (plus their containers and attachments). Never modify a source file.
3. **Classify** each result by its `executionType` label, cross-checked with its source: a result from `reports/smoke/**` must say `smoke`, one from a regression archive must say `regression`. A result with `unknown` or a contradicting label stops the build with `AMBIGUOUS <n> result(s): <specFile> <testCaseId> (<source>)` and the advice to rerun through the run scripts or pass the run's type explicitly with `--runs <RunId>=<type>` after the user confirms it. Never guess. Never put the same result in both sections.
4. **Group regression by epic, then story.** The epic comes from the `epic` label (cross-checked with the `workbook` label and the `specFile` folder; a contradiction stops the build like an ambiguous type). Story IDs and names come from the `storyId` / `storyName` labels. Only executed results count: no hardcoded list, no epic or story without results. A regression result without an epic (a flat legacy spec with no `WORKBOOK`) stops the build with `NO EPIC <n> result(s): <specFile> <testCaseId>` and the advice to move the spec into its workbook folder or rerun through the run scripts; it is never guessed or dropped silently.
5. **Select the results that represent each test.**
   - Single run: keep every result of that run, retries included, exactly as recorded.
   - Snapshot: identity = workbook (when known) + `specFile` + `platform` + `environment` + `testCaseId` (+ the full test name when a spec has no ID). For each identity keep the attempts of the latest run by its start time; never merge two tests only because their IDs match. Count raw result files, retried attempts and distinct testcases separately.
   - A smoke run whose `run.json` says `runType: partial` or whose decision is `INCONCLUSIVE` is labelled "partial smoke run" wherever it appears.
6. **Make sanitized copies** in a temporary folder, from which Allure generates (the source folders stay untouched):
   - keep: names, statuses, status details' first line (passed through the project's `Redactor`), start/stop timestamps, labels (`epic`, `feature`, `story`, `tms`, `testCaseId`, `storyId`, `specFile`, `executionType`, `runId`, `platform`, `environment`, `workbook`, `severity`), links to requirements, step names (redacted);
   - drop: parameters whose name or value looks sensitive (password, pin, otp, token, secret, auth, cookie, email, mobile, phone, account, card) and every other parameter value, `statusDetails.trace` (stack), `logger/` content, page sources, driver request/response bodies, the `Logger` per-test log attachment, any attachment that is not an image;
   - screenshots: excluded by default. With `--include-screenshots`, include only images listed in `report/screenshot-review.json` (`{ "<attachment source>": "reviewed" }`), written after a person reviewed each one for credentials, OTPs, personal data and other apps; any other image is dropped and counted;
   - categories: write `categories.json` with "Product defect candidate (needs triage)" for failed assertions, "Automation / environment" for broken tests and `Skip`, "Blocked" for `BlockedError`. A failed assertion is never labelled a confirmed product defect;
   - `environment.properties` with application, platform, environment, execution type, run IDs and date range; `executor.json` naming `report:share` (not a CI build) unless the run metadata names one.
7. **Generate** with the local CLI: `npx allure generate <sanitized scope> --single-file --clean -o <section folder>` when `--single-file` is supported; otherwise `npx allure generate <scope> --clean -o <section folder>` and write in README and on the dashboard that the multi-file report must be served over HTTP (for example `npx allure open report/smoke`), because browsers block it from `file://`. Never edit generated Allure HTML.
7a. **One Allure report per epic:** generate `regression/<WorkbookFolder>/index.html` from the sanitized results of that epic only, all its stories together (step 7 rules).
8. **Write `regression/index.html`**: one row per epic: epic (workbook) name, stories executed out of the stories in the workbook when the workbook is readable ("Partial epic" when fewer), the executed story IDs and names, distinct testcases, status totals, raw results, retries, run IDs / date range, and a relative link `./<WorkbookFolder>/index.html` with each path segment percent-encoded (`encodeURIComponent`: spaces become `%20`). Newest epic run first.
9. **Write `index.html`** (plain HTML and CSS, responsive, no external resources): application and platform; the actual execution date range and time zone; scope ("single run" or "snapshot of N runs"); links to `smoke/index.html` and `regression/index.html`; status totals calculated from the included results; warnings: partial coverage (eligible P0 cases missing in the smoke manifest, stories in the workbook with no executed results), partial or INCONCLUSIVE smoke runs, snapshots of older runs, omitted diagnostic detail, omitted screenshots. It never says "all passed", "release ready" or "tests were rerun" unless the numbers show exactly that, and never presents partial coverage as complete regression or sign-off.
10. **Write `report-scope.json`**:

```json
{
  "generator": "report:share",
  "generatedAt": "<ISO>", "timeZone": "<IANA or Windows id>",
  "application": "<name>", "platforms": ["android"], "environments": ["qa"],
  "allure": { "version": "<x.y.z>", "singleFile": true },
  "sourceMode": "latest | archive",
  "runSelectionPolicy": "<sentence describing the rule actually used>",
  "sources": [{ "runId": "...", "executionType": "regression", "path": "test-results/allure-archive/...", "rawResults": 0, "startedAt": "...", "finishedAt": "..." }],
  "observedRange": { "from": "<ISO>", "to": "<ISO>" },
  "counts": {
    "smoke": { "sourceResults": 0, "includedResults": 0, "retriedAttempts": 0, "distinctTestcases": 0, "status": { "passed": 0, "failed": 0, "broken": 0, "skipped": 0, "unknown": 0 } },
    "regression": { "sourceResults": 0, "includedResults": 0, "retriedAttempts": 0, "distinctTestcases": 0, "status": { } }
  },
  "epics": [{ "epic": "<WorkbookFolder>", "workbook": "<WorkbookFolder>.xlsx", "folder": "regression/<WorkbookFolder>/", "storiesInWorkbook": 0, "partial": false,
              "stories": [{ "storyId": "US002", "storyName": "...", "distinctTestcases": 0, "includedResults": 0, "status": { } }],
              "distinctTestcases": 0, "includedResults": 0, "status": { } }],
  "warnings": ["..."],
  "omitted": { "stackTraces": true, "logs": true, "pageSources": true, "parameters": 0, "unreviewedScreenshots": 0 }
}
```

11. **Write `README.md`**: what each folder is, how to open it (extract the ZIP, open `index.html`; single-file reports open directly from disk only when that was verified in step 13, otherwise serve the folder), how to share (the ZIP only), the scope and selection policy in plain words, the omitted detail, and the limitations ("not a release sign-off", "a failed assertion is a candidate, not a confirmed defect").
12. **ZIP** `<Application>-Allure-Reports-<YYYY-MM-DD>.zip` (date = generation date, `--date` to override): `index.html`, `README.md`, `report-scope.json`, `smoke/`, `regression/` and each epic folder, with relative paths preserved. Nothing else: no raw results, no sanitized temp files, no older ZIPs, no `allure-report/`.
13. **Self-check** before swapping the new `report/` in: every local link in the generated HTML pages resolves; each epic report's results all carry that `epic` and no other, and every executed story of the epic is in it; the dashboard and index counts equal `report-scope.json`; every included attachment file exists; ZIP entries equal the planned list; the sanitized copies contain no value matched by the `Redactor` patterns. Any failure stops the build with the reason.

## 5. Bootstrap

- Add the labels of section 2 to the shared hooks (Mobile) and base fixture (Web).
- Add `scripts/report/build-share-report.mjs`, `scripts/report/run-regression.mjs` (`npm run test:regression`), their fixture tests, `npm run report:share` and `npm run report:share:test`, and `report/` to `.gitignore`.
- Fixture tests (small synthetic `*-result.json` sets, no Allure binary needed except one optional smoke test that runs only when `npx allure --version` works): classification by label, refusal on `unknown` or contradicting labels, a result counted in only one section, one epic folder per executed workbook holding all its stories (two workbooks → two folders, no per-story folders), a subset run labelled partial epic, `NO EPIC` refusal, percent-encoded links for folder names with spaces, snapshot selection by identity and run time (two specs sharing an ID stay separate), retries counted apart from distinct testcases, partial smoke labelled, sanitization (parameters, stacks, logs, non-image attachments, unreviewed screenshots removed), counts in `report-scope.json`, refusal to overwrite a foreign `report/`, ZIP entry list.
- Do not generate a real report at bootstrap (no results exist yet).

## 6. Validation when reports are generated (report:share run by an agent)

Open `report/index.html`, the snapshot's `index.html`, `smoke/index.html`, `regression/index.html` and every epic report in a browser, and confirm: the counts shown match `report-scope.json`; each epic report shows only its own epic and all of its executed stories under Behaviors; included screenshots load; every link works; the ZIP extracts and its `index.html` opens. State plainly whether the reports opened from `file://` or needed a local server. Run `npm run lint` and `npm run report:share:test` for any change to the generator. Report output paths, scope, validation results and limitations. Never upload the reports anywhere.
